newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Minister sees no pay mutiny in Russian forces.
newsitem.headline: Minister sees no pay mutiny in Russian forces.

text.p: Russia's armed forces are unlikely to revolt over unpaid wages, Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov said on Wednesday, adding that he saw no need for a state of emergency as President Boris Yeltsin recovered from surgery.
Kulikov's interior ministry troops and other forces, including the army, have suffered serious delays in pay. Low morale has been compounded by the debacle in breakaway Chechnya.
Kulikov told a news conference that wage delays for interior ministry troops were running at between one and two months.
Sacked Kremlin security adviser Alexander Lebed, a bitter political enemy of Kulikov, has warned the army could mutiny over the lack of funds.
Kulikov conceded it was a cause of tension but that he and other ministers were working to solve the problem.
"Knowing that this (the pay problem) will be settled, it wouldn't be right to forecast such a revolt," Kulikov said.
Worries over instability in Russia reached a peak as Yeltsin underwent multiple heart bypass surgery on Tuesday.
Kulikov told the news conference, organised by Interfax news agency, that he wished Yeltsin a speedy recovery and said he saw no civil unrest or emergency situations.
"There is absolutely no need for the introduction of a state of emergency," Kulikov said, noting that Yeltsin had formally taken back power from his prime minister early on Wednesday.
